label: L-01
title: Shared UniPoolerCutoverCore step 2 has no recovery branch: a 2-wei donate+sync on the permissionless canonical sUSDS/phUSD pair makes the mainnet cutover core revert for good
fingerprintVerified: re-derived by finding-manager as sha256(contract:function:rootCauseClass:entryPoint); matches verbatim
description: Core step 2 requires the canonical pair's reserves to be (0,0) both before and after an optional skim, and there is no other branch. Uniswap V2 reserves set by sync() can never return to (0,0) once LP totalSupply is 0: skim() does not touch reserves and burn() needs LP. yield-claim-nft:051's constructor check (UniPoolerV2__PairNotCanonical) binds UniPoolerV2 to factory.getPair(sUSDS, phUSD), so the pooler cannot be pointed at a different pair. Any third party can therefore createPair today (mainnet getPair == 0 at block 26109485), transfer 1 wei of each token and call sync(). After that, every run of the shared core reverts at step 2. The core is inherited by the dev rehearsal (story 101) and by the future mainnet cutover script and fork test (story 103), so this defect propagates to the mainnet operation. docs/BalancerWinddownPlan.md §4 (lines 410-414) discusses only in-window griefing between steps 1 and 6, and points to a recovery helper (transfer + pair.mint(UniPoolerV2) with a price check) that does not exist in the core. Pre-emptive poisoning before the run starts is not addressed.
impact: Availability of the Balancexit index-4 cutover, not funds. The revert happens in forge's simulation, before any broadcast, so nothing is half-done. But the 103 script as built on this core cannot run at all until someone writes, reviews and broadcasts a bespoke seeding path under the Balancer wind-down timeline. The griefer's cost is 2 wei plus gas. A recovery exists outside the core (send the recovered tokens to the pair, then pair.mint(newPooler): with LP totalSupply 0 the first minter takes all LP and the griefer's dust is absorbed), which caps severity at Low.
evidence: side-effects.json mainnetForkProbe.tests[1] (test_B_dustSyncedPairPermanentlyBlocksCoreStep2 PASS at block 26109485: reserves (1,1) after sync, pair totalSupply 0, unchanged after skim, core reverts 'UniPoolerCutoverCore: pair reserves not empty'); live read getPair(sUSDS, phUSD) == 0x0. Test A (same file) shows the core otherwise completes on live state.
attackPath: 2. Griefer calls factory.createPair(sUSDS, phUSD), transfers 1 wei of each token to the pair, then calls pair.sync(). Reserves become (1,1) and LP totalSupply stays 0.
3. skim() does not change reserves and burn() needs LP, so reserves can never return to (0,0). UniPoolerV2's constructor (UniPoolerV2__PairNotCanonical) rules out using any other pair.

4. Every run of UniPoolerCutoverCore reverts at _step2EnsurePairEmpty with 'UniPoolerCutoverCore: pair reserves not empty' in forge's simulation (work/test/audit-run39/UniPoolerCoreMainnetFork.t.sol::test_B_dustSyncedPairPermanentlyBlocksCoreStep2 PASS on a mainnet fork; reproduced by the orchestrator).
5. The owner has to write, review and broadcast a different seeding path before the 103 cutover can run. That delays the migration, but no value is lost.

classification.assetImpact: No assets are at risk. The revert happens in forge's local simulation of core step 2, before any broadcast, so nothing is half-executed and the recovered sUSDS/phUSD never leave the Balancer position. The impact is availability of an operational migration: the story-103 cutover, as built on this core, cannot run once the canonical pair has been dust-synced. Meanwhile index-4 keeps working on BalancerPoolerV2 (configs(4) is unchanged and unpaused). After 30 Oct pool() reverts and accrued sUSDS just sits idle. After 30 Nov the proportional recovery exit still works (BalancerWinddownPlan.md L16-38, L250). The pair is not unusable. With reserves (1,1) and totalSupply 0, UniswapV2Pair.mint still credits amount = balance - reserve and grants the first minter sqrt(a0*a1) - MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY, so an atomic transfer+mint absorbs the dust at our ratio. Only the core's strict reserves==0 require blocks.

classification.likelihood: medium. The action is permissionless, costs 2 wei plus gas, and the window is open today. A griefer gains nothing except the delay.
classification.assumptions: Index-4 stays functional on BalancerPoolerV2 while the cutover is delayed (confirmed: configs(4) unchanged and unpaused). Balancer's proportional recovery exit stays available after the 30 Oct and 30 Nov pauses (BIP-928, BalancerWinddownPlan.md L38). The fix is a script change, with no redeploy of any protocol contract.

justification: Rated Low, not Medium. It is flagged for human review because the sanitizer argued for Medium. The case for Medium is a cheap, permissionless and permanent DoS of a mainnet-bound migration core, which is a fair Law-1 availability argument, and nothing here dismisses it. It still falls short of C4 Medium for four reasons. (1) No asset is at risk, and protocol function is not impaired: index-4 mints keep working on BalancerPoolerV2, and the Balancer exit stays open through recovery mode after both BIP-928 deadlines, so the delay costs at most idle sUSDS (opportunity cost), not principal. (2) The revert is fail-loud in simulation before any broadcast, so nothing is half-wired. (3) 'Permanent' applies only to the strict require in this script core, not to the pair. An atomic transfer+mint seed absorbs the dust, and once LP totalSupply > 0 further dust-syncs cannot block a mint-based seed, so the grief cannot be repeated against the fix. (4) The workaround is a script-level change, and the wind-down plan already describes it (for the post-step-2 case). The gap was also already raised in story 108's own review as a [Low-Medium, doc] finding and accepted non-blocking by the human. This is disclosed for transparency; that review is not a ledger disposition, so it does not suppress this finding, and the finding stays open because the core still has no branch for it. Re-weigh to Medium if index-4 or the Balancer exit stops working while the cutover is blocked, or if the deadline pressure becomes a value loss rather than a delay. The check itself is load-bearing: Router02.addLiquidity quotes against existing reserves, so any relaxation that seeds through the router would let the griefer choose the opening price. The recommendation keeps that protection.
recommendation: Add a pre-poisoned-pair branch to the core instead of relaxing the router path. When reserves != 0 AND pair.totalSupply() == 0, do NOT seed through Router02, because it would quote against griefer-set reserves. Instead, from ONE transaction via a small reviewed helper contract (never two owner txs, since anyone can call pair.mint(to) after a bare transfer and take all the LP), transfer all recovered sUSDS/phUSD to the pair, call pair.mint(newPooler), and then require: (a) the post-mint reserve ratio is within seedToleranceBps of the Balancer exit ratio (sAmt:pAmt), (b) the pre-existing reserves are below an explicit dust bound, and (c) newPooler holds totalSupply - MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY. Keep the strict (0,0) path when totalSupply == 0 and reserves == 0. Revert, as today, when totalSupply > 0 or the reserves exceed the dust bound. Better still, do createPair-if-missing, the skim check and the transfer+mint seed atomically in the helper, which also closes the step-2-to-6 window. Add a core unit test that pre-syncs (1,1) and expects the branch to succeed with the ratio check enforced, plus a test where a large skewed pre-sync fails the ratio check. Land it in the shared core before the story-103 broadcast.

quotes: Preconditions `require`d: authorized-pooler set revoked (story 099); pair absent or reserves (0,0)
createPair is permissionless, so a griefer can donate+sync between creation and seeding to break the (0,0) precondition — follow the mitigation phStaging2:108 documents.
**[Low-Medium, doc] No recovery path if the step 2 empty-pair `require` fails.** A donation plus `sync()` before step 2 leaves the canonical pair permanently non-empty

The human accepted all findings as non-blocking, including the Medium finding (unsynced one-sided donation between Stage 2 steps 2 and 6 is not harmless) and the Low-Medium finding (no recovery path if the step 2 empty-pair require fails).
